page.overview:
Who is Galadriel?

Galadriel was the Ñoldorin Lady of the woods of Lothlórien who witnessed Middle-earth during the three Ages of Awakening.

Galadriel was born in Aman as one of the Ñoldor. She was the daughter of Finarfin and Eärwen, and younger sister of Finrod, Angrod, and Aegnor. She took part in the Exile of the Ñoldor, following Fëanor in his rebellion. However, she opposed the Kinslaying at Alqualondë and crossed the Helcaraxë with the rest of Fingolfin's followers. After arriving in Beleriand, she lived mainly in Doriath, where she befriended Melian. Later, with her husband Celeborn, she ruled over the woodland Elves of Lothlórien, and together they had a daughter, Celebrían, who married Elrond.

She is described as "the mightiest and fairest of all the Elves that remained in Middle-earth", and the "greatest of Elven women". Throughout the Third Age it was unknown who wielded the Three Rings, but during the War of the Ring, Galadriel revealed to Frodo Baggins that she was the bearer of Nenya. After the War, she returned to the Uttermost West.

Galadriel was born in Eldamar in the year 1362 of the Trees of the First Age. She was the fourth child of Finarfin, prince of the Ñoldor, who named her Artanis. Her mother was Eärwen, princess of the Falmari, who named her Nerwen. Galadriel grew beautiful and tall, even for the women of the Ñoldor. Being strong of body, will, and mind, she was "a match for both the loremasters and the athletes of the Eldar in the days of their youth".
